Original explanatory text written for this app
policy: The v1.2 content policy applies, as everywhere in the app.

lessons.title: What Vedic astrology is
sections: A map of the sky

A birth chart (kundli) is a map of where the Sun, the Moon and the planets were, seen from your birthplace, at the moment you were born. Vedic astrology (Jyotish) reads that map to describe tendencies in character and the timing of life's chapters.
The sidereal zodiac

Vedic astrology measures the zodiac against the fixed stars (the sidereal zodiac). Western astrology uses the seasons instead, so the two differ by about 24 degrees today; that is why your Vedic Sun sign is often one sign earlier than your Western one. The difference is called the ayanamsa; this app uses the Lahiri ayanamsa, the standard in India.
Parashari astrology
The main school, used throughout this app, comes from the Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra (BPHS). Other systems in the app, such as KP, Tajika and Lal Kitab, are labelled separately.
Tendencies, not fate
A chart shows inclinations and favourable or testing periods. Your choices, effort and circumstances shape how they play out. Read the chart as a weather forecast, not a verdict.
The four parts of a reading

Every reading combines four things: the signs (how something is expressed), the planets (what acts), the houses (where in life it shows) and the dashas (when it comes up). Every screen in this app works with these four, and the lessons follow the same order.
What you need to cast a chart

The date, the exact time and the place of birth. The time matters most: the rising sign changes about every two hours and the houses change with it. If the birth time is uncertain by more than a few minutes, read the house-based results with care; the Moon sign and the nakshatra are more reliable.
The classical books

Besides BPHS, the app draws on Brihat Jataka by Varahamihira, Saravali by Kalyanavarma, Phaladeepika by Mantreswara and Jataka Parijata. Where they disagree, the app follows BPHS or notes the difference.

lessons.title: The 12 signs (Rashis)
sections: Twelve parts of the sky
The zodiac is a circle of 360 degrees split into twelve signs of 30 degrees each, from Aries (Mesha) to Pisces (Meena). A sign is the 'flavour' of a placement: how a planet expresses itself.
Element

Each sign belongs to an element. Fire (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius): energy and initiative. Earth (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn): practicality and stability. Air (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius): thought and connection. Water (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces): feeling and sensitivity.
Quality
Movable signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn) start things; fixed signs (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius) hold steady; dual signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces) adapt.
Ruler

Every sign has a ruling planet: Mars rules Aries and Scorpio; Venus rules Taurus and Libra; Mercury rules Gemini and Virgo; the Moon rules Cancer; the Sun rules Leo; Jupiter rules Sagittarius and Pisces; Saturn rules Capricorn and Aquarius. The ruler of a sign is called its lord.
Odd and even signs
Odd signs (Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, Aquarius) are masculine: outgoing and active. Even signs (Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, Pisces) are feminine: receptive and steady.
The signs one by one

Aries: bold, quick, pioneering. Taurus: steady, sensual, practical. Gemini: curious, talkative, versatile. Cancer: caring, protective, emotional. Leo: proud, generous, a natural leader. Virgo: precise, helpful, analytical. Libra: fair, social, artistic. Scorpio: intense, private, determined. Sagittarius: idealistic, frank, a seeker. Capricorn: patient, ambitious, dutiful. Aquarius: independent, humane, unconventional. Pisces: gentle, imaginative, spiritual.
Sanskrit names

Mesha (Aries), Vrishabha (Taurus), Mithuna (Gemini), Karka (Cancer), Simha (Leo), Kanya (Virgo), Tula (Libra), Vrishchika (Scorpio), Dhanu (Sagittarius), Makara (Capricorn), Kumbha (Aquarius), Meena (Pisces).
Directions

The fire signs belong to the east, the earth signs to the south, the air signs to the west and the water signs to the north. The directions are used in Vastu, in Prashna and when choosing which way to face for a practice.

lessons.title: The 9 planets (Grahas)
sections: Nine grahas

Vedic astrology uses seven visible planets (the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn) and the two lunar nodes, Rahu and Ketu, the points where the Moon's path crosses the Sun's. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto are not used.
What each one stands for

The Sun: self, vitality, authority, father. The Moon: mind, feelings, mother, comfort. Mars: energy, courage, siblings, property. Mercury: intellect, speech, trade. Jupiter: wisdom, teachers, faith, growth. Venus: love, beauty, comfort, partnership. Saturn: discipline, work, patience, delay. Rahu: ambition, the unusual and the foreign. Ketu: detachment, insight, letting go.
Natural benefics and malefics

Jupiter, Venus, a well-placed Mercury and a bright (waxing) Moon are natural benefics: they tend to give easily. The Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rahu and Ketu are natural malefics: they tend to test and push. A 'malefic' is not bad; it gives through effort.
The Moon and the Ascendant
The rising sign shows the body and the way you meet life; the Moon shows the mind. That is why Vedic astrology often reads the chart from both.
Natural friends and enemies

BPHS gives each planet natural friends, neutrals and enemies. The Sun's friends are the Moon, Mars and Jupiter; Venus and Saturn are its enemies. The Moon has no enemies; the Sun and Mercury are its friends. Mars is friendly to the Sun, Moon and Jupiter and unfriendly to Mercury. Mercury likes the Sun and Venus and dislikes the Moon. Jupiter likes the Sun, Moon and Mars and dislikes Mercury and Venus. Venus likes Mercury and Saturn and dislikes the Sun and Moon. Saturn likes Mercury and Venus and dislikes the Sun, Moon and Mars. A planet in a friend's sign is at ease; in an enemy's sign it struggles.
Days and colours

Each planet rules a weekday and a colour: the Sun Sunday and copper-red, the Moon Monday and white, Mars Tuesday and red, Mercury Wednesday and green, Jupiter Thursday and yellow, Venus Friday and bright white, Saturn Saturday and dark blue or black. Rahu and Ketu have no day of their own and are usually honoured on Saturday. These are used in remedies and in choosing a good day.
Natural significators (karakas)

Each planet stands for certain people and things in every chart: the Sun for the father and the soul, the Moon for the mother and the mind, Mars for brothers, courage and land, Mercury for speech and learning, Jupiter for teachers, wisdom and wealth, Venus for the spouse, comforts and the arts, Saturn for work, servants and discipline, Rahu for foreign things and ambition, and Ketu for detachment and spiritual release.
Fast and slow planets

The Moon goes round the zodiac in about 27 days, the Sun in a year, Mercury and Venus stay near the Sun, Mars takes about two years, Jupiter about twelve, Saturn about thirty, and Rahu and Ketu about eighteen and a half, always moving backwards through the signs.

lessons.title: The 12 houses (Bhavas)
sections: Twelve areas of life

The rising sign (Lagna) becomes the 1st house, the next sign the 2nd, and so on. Each house is an area of life: 1 self and body; 2 money, family, speech; 3 courage, effort, siblings, short journeys; 4 home, mother, comfort, property; 5 learning, creativity, romance; 6 work, service, rivals, health habits; 7 marriage and partners; 8 sudden changes, research, shared money; 9 luck, father, teachers, faith; 10 career and status; 11 gains, income, friends; 12 expenses, rest, foreign lands, letting go.
House groups

Kendras (1, 4, 7, 10) are the pillars: planets there act strongly. Trikonas (1, 5, 9) are the houses of fortune. Dusthanas (6, 8, 12) are the testing houses. Upachayas (3, 6, 10, 11) are houses of growth, where even difficult planets improve with time.
Empty houses
An empty house is not a bad house. It is judged by its lord: where that planet sits and how strong it is.
Reading from the Moon too
Vedic astrology also counts the houses from the Moon's sign (Chandra Lagna). A result promised from both the Lagna and the Moon is much more reliable. Transits are read mainly from the Moon.
Bhavat bhavam: house from house

Counting a house as many houses from itself as its own number repeats its theme: the 4th from the 4th is the 7th, the 9th from the 9th is the 5th, the 10th from the 10th is the 7th. So the 7th also carries something of the 4th and the 10th.
The four aims of life

The houses are grouped by the four aims of life: dharma (purpose) 1, 5, 9; artha (wealth) 2, 6, 10; kama (desire) 3, 7, 11; moksha (release) 4, 8, 12. A chart heavy in one group shows what the person is drawn to.
Strong and weak houses

A house is strong when its lord is strong and well placed, when benefics occupy or aspect it, and when it is a kendra or trikona. It is weaker when its lord falls in a dusthana or is debilitated or combust, or when only malefics aspect it.

lessons.title: Reading the chart picture
sections: Two ways to draw one chart

A birth chart is drawn as a square picture with twelve boxes, one for each house. Two styles are common, and this app can draw both: the North Indian chart (a diamond pattern) and the South Indian chart (a ring of squares). They hold exactly the same information. Bengal also uses an East Indian style, which this app does not draw; like the South Indian one, it keeps the signs in fixed boxes. You can switch style on the Chart Diagram screen.
North Indian: the houses stay in place

In the North Indian chart the boxes are the houses, and they never move. The diamond at the top centre is always the 1st house (the Lagna). From there the houses run anticlockwise: the 2nd is the triangle to its upper left, the 3rd the triangle below that, the 4th the diamond on the left, and so on round to the 12th, the triangle to the upper right of the Lagna. The four diamonds are the kendras: 1st at the top, 4th on the left, 7th at the bottom and 10th on the right.
north_template
The small numbers are signs

In the North Indian chart the small number in each box is the sign in that house, counted from Aries: 1 Aries, 2 Taurus, 3 Gemini, 4 Cancer, 5 Leo, 6 Virgo, 7 Libra, 8 Scorpio, 9 Sagittarius, 10 Capricorn, 11 Aquarius, 12 Pisces. So the number in the top diamond tells you the rising sign: a 6 there means Virgo rising. The numbers go up by one as you go anticlockwise. Beginners often mistake these numbers for house numbers; the house is the position of the box, the number is the sign.
South Indian: the signs stay in place

In the South Indian chart the boxes are the signs, and they never move. Pisces is the top-left box, Aries the next one to the right, and the signs run clockwise round the edge to Aquarius below Pisces. The four middle boxes are left empty. The rising sign is marked: in this app its box has a bold border and the word ASC. To find any house, start at the marked box as the 1st and count clockwise.
south_template
The planets

Planets are written as short names: Su Sun, Mo Moon, Ma Mars, Me Mercury, Ju Jupiter, Ve Venus, Sa Saturn, Ra Rahu, Ke Ketu, and ASC for the Ascendant. Planets in the same box share a house and a sign; they are conjunct and colour each other. Rahu and Ketu are always in opposite boxes, seven houses apart. An empty box simply has no planet; it is read through its lord.
Divisional charts
The Navamsa (D9) and the other divisional charts are drawn the same way, with their own rising sign. Read them with the same steps: find the Lagna, then count the houses from it.

lessons.title: House lords: how areas connect
sections: Every house has a lord
The lord of a house is the ruler of the sign on that house. If Gemini is on your 10th house, Mercury is your 10th lord.
Where the lord goes, the house goes

A lord carries its house's matters to the house it sits in. A 10th lord (career) in the 7th house (partners) often links work with partnership or the public. This one idea, linking two houses through their lord, explains much of a chart.
Good and difficult lordships

Lords of trikonas (1, 5, 9) are helpful for any rising sign; lords of dusthanas (6, 8, 12) bring their tests wherever they go. A planet that rules both a kendra and a trikona is a Yogakaraka, an especially helpful planet for that rising sign.
The Lagna lord matters most
The lord of the 1st house stands for the person. Its sign, house and strength colour the whole chart: a strong Lagna lord in a good house supports everything else.
Exchange of signs (Parivartana)

When two lords sit in each other's signs, for example the 10th lord in the 4th and the 4th lord in the 10th, the two houses are tied together strongly, as if each lord were in its own sign. Exchanges between good houses form a strong yoga; exchanges with a dusthana mix the results.
Yogakarakas by rising sign
Saturn is the yogakaraka for Taurus and Libra rising, Mars for Cancer and Leo, and Venus for Capricorn and Aquarius. The other rising signs have no single planet ruling both a kendra and a trikona.

lessons.title: Strength and dignity
sections: Exaltation and debilitation

Each planet has a sign where it is strongest (exalted) and the opposite sign where it is weakest (debilitated). The Sun is exalted in Aries, the Moon in Taurus, Mars in Capricorn, Mercury in Virgo, Jupiter in Cancer, Venus in Pisces and Saturn in Libra.
Own sign and friends
A planet in its own sign is comfortable and reliable. In a friend's sign it is at ease; in an enemy's sign it works harder.
Retrograde and combust

A retrograde planet appears to move backwards; its results tend to come through review, repetition or an inward route. A planet very close to the Sun is combust: its light is hidden, so it can feel weaker or less visible.
Cancellation
A debilitated planet can recover (Neecha Bhanga) when, for example, the lord of its sign sits in a kendra. Weakness in one place is rarely the whole story.
Moolatrikona signs

Between its exaltation and its own sign, each planet has a moolatrikona sign where it works especially well: the Sun Leo, the Moon Taurus, Mars Aries, Mercury Virgo, Jupiter Sagittarius, Venus Libra and Saturn Aquarius.
Exact exaltation degrees

Exaltation is strongest at one degree: the Sun at 10 degrees Aries, the Moon at 3 Taurus, Mars at 28 Capricorn, Mercury at 15 Virgo, Jupiter at 5 Cancer, Venus at 27 Pisces and Saturn at 20 Libra. Debilitation is deepest at the same degree of the opposite sign.
Directional strength (Dig bala)
Planets also gain strength in certain houses: Jupiter and Mercury in the 1st, the Sun and Mars in the 10th, Saturn in the 7th, and the Moon and Venus in the 4th.
How close is combust?
BPHS gives the distance from the Sun at which each planet becomes combust: the Moon 12 degrees, Mars 17, Mercury 14 (12 when retrograde), Jupiter 11, Venus 10 (8 when retrograde) and Saturn 15.

lessons.title: Aspects (Drishti)
sections: Planets look at houses
In Vedic astrology every planet aspects (looks at) the 7th house from itself. Mars also aspects the 4th and 8th, Jupiter the 5th and 9th, and Saturn the 3rd and 10th.
Why it matters
An aspect brings the planet's nature to that house. Jupiter's aspect protects and expands; Saturn's slows and makes you work for it; Mars's adds energy and heat.
Rahu and Ketu
Texts differ on the nodes' aspects. This app counts only their 7th-house aspect; some astrologers also give them the 5th and 9th.
Full and partial aspects

The classical texts also give partial aspects (a quarter, a half or three quarters) to other houses. The app, like most modern practice, counts only the full aspects: the 7th for everyone plus the special ones of Mars, Jupiter and Saturn.
Mutual aspects

When two planets aspect each other, for example from opposite houses, they exchange influence. Jupiter and the Moon in mutual aspect form a Gajakesari-like support; Saturn and Mars in mutual aspect add pressure to both houses.
Aspects in the picture
Open the Chart picture guide in this screen to see how to find aspects on the chart itself by counting boxes.

lessons.title: Nakshatras: the lunar mansions
sections: 27 star groups
The zodiac is also divided into 27 nakshatras of 13 degrees 20 minutes each, starting with Ashwini. Each has a ruling planet, a deity and a character, and is split into four quarters (padas).
Your birth star
The nakshatra of your Moon is your birth star (janma nakshatra). It colours the mind and the emotional nature, and it is used to match charts for marriage.
The key to timing
The ruler of your Moon's nakshatra decides the first period of the Vimshottari dasha you were born into, and how much of it was left at birth.
The 27 nakshatras

Ashwini, Bharani, Krittika, Rohini, Mrigashira, Ardra, Punarvasu, Pushya, Ashlesha, Magha, Purva Phalguni, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Vishakha, Anuradha, Jyeshtha, Mula, Purva Ashadha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Purva Bhadrapada, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati.
Their lords

The nakshatra lords repeat in a fixed cycle of nine, three times round the zodiac: Ketu, Venus, the Sun, the Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury. Ashwini, Magha and Mula are Ketu's; Bharani, Purva Phalguni and Purva Ashadha are Venus's; and so on. This is the same order as the Vimshottari dasha.
Padas and the Navamsa
Each nakshatra has four padas of 3 degrees 20 minutes, 108 in all, and each pada is exactly one navamsa. That is why the pada of the Moon or the Lagna tells you its Navamsa sign.
Ganas
Each nakshatra has a temperament (gana): divine (deva), human (manushya) or fierce (rakshasa). The gana is used, with other factors, when matching charts for marriage.

lessons.title: Yogas: special combinations
sections: What a yoga is
A yoga is a specific combination of planets, signs or house lords that classical texts link to a particular result.
Some well-known yogas

Gajakesari: Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon (respect, good sense). Raja Yoga: lords of a kendra and a trikona connected (rise in status). Pancha Mahapurusha: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn in its own or exaltation sign in a kendra from the Lagna (a strong, distinctive personality).
A yoga needs strength
A yoga works fully only when the planets forming it are strong and unafflicted, and it shows most in their periods. Many charts have several yogas; their presence alone is not a promise.
Raja yogas
A Raja Yoga forms when a kendra lord and a trikona lord join, aspect each other or exchange signs. It promises rise and recognition, mostly in the periods of the planets that form it.
Dhana yogas
Dhana yogas link the lords of the wealth houses (2nd, 5th, 9th and 11th) with each other or with the Lagna lord. They show the capacity to earn and keep money.
Viparita Raja yogas

When the lords of the 6th, 8th or 12th fall into another of these houses, a difficulty cancels a difficulty and the person rises after setbacks. The three are Harsha (6th lord), Sarala (8th lord) and Vimala (12th lord).
Challenging combinations

Some combinations are traditionally difficult, such as Kemadruma (no planet on either side of the Moon) or Kuja Dosha. Most have classical cancellations, and the app checks them before naming a dosha. Kala Sarpa is a later idea, not found in BPHS.

lessons.title: Dashas: the timing of life
sections: Planetary periods
The Vimshottari dasha divides a 120-year cycle among the nine planets: Ketu 7 years, Venus 20, the Sun 6, the Moon 10, Mars 7, Rahu 18, Jupiter 16, Saturn 19 and Mercury 17, always in that order.
Main and sub-periods
Each main period (Mahadasha) is divided into sub-periods (Antardashas) of all nine planets in the same order. The main period sets the background; the sub-period sets the current focus.
How to read a period

A period brings out what its planet promises in your chart: the houses it rules, the house it sits in, its strength and the yogas it joins. A well-placed planet's period tends to go smoothly; a troubled one's asks for more care.
Working out a sub-period

The length of an Antardasha is the main period's years times the sub-period planet's years, divided by 120. In Saturn's 19-year Mahadasha, the Mercury Antardasha lasts 19 x 17 / 120, about 2 years 8 months.
Smaller periods
Each Antardasha is again divided into nine Pratyantardashas in the same order, which help with timing to the month.
Changing periods
The months around a change of Mahadasha (dasha sandhi) often feel unsettled, as one theme closes and another opens. They are a time for patience, not alarm.
Other dasha systems

Vimshottari is the main system, but there are others. The app also gives Yogini dasha (36-year cycle) and Jaimini's Char dasha on the More Dashas screen; agreement between systems strengthens a prediction.

lessons.title: Transits (Gochara)
sections: Planets on the move
Transits are where the planets are now, compared with your birth chart. In Vedic astrology they are mainly read from your Moon sign.
Slow planets matter most

Saturn spends about two and a half years in a sign, Jupiter about a year, and Rahu and Ketu about eighteen months, so their transits mark longer phases. The Moon moves through a sign in about two and a half days.
Sade Sati
Sade Sati is the roughly seven and a half years when Saturn passes through the sign before your Moon, your Moon sign and the sign after. It is a period of responsibility and maturing, not a disaster.
Dasha first
Transits trigger what the dashas promise. A good transit in a difficult period helps a little; a testing transit in a good period is usually mild.
Transits and Ashtakavarga
A planet transiting a sign with many Ashtakavarga points (bindus) gives better results than one transiting a sign with few. The Ashtakavarga screen shows the points for each sign.
Saturn's small panoti
Saturn's transit of the 4th or the 8th sign from the Moon (dhaiya, about two and a half years each) is also watched, like Sade Sati, as a time to slow down and be careful.
Retrograde transits
When a slow planet turns retrograde it can move back into the previous sign, so its transit effects return for a while. Matters started then often need revisiting.

lessons.title: Divisional charts (Vargas)
sections: Charts within the chart
Each sign can be divided into smaller parts to make divisional charts that focus on one area of life. The birth chart is D1.
The Navamsa (D9)

The Navamsa divides each sign into nine parts. It is the most important divisional chart: it shows the inner strength of each planet and is read for marriage and the second half of life. A planet strong in both D1 and D9 is reliable.
Vargottama
A planet in the same sign in D1 and D9 is vargottama, which classical texts count as a source of strength.
Other vargas
D10 (Dashamsa) is read for career, D2 for wealth, D4 for property and D12 for parents.
What each varga shows

D2 Hora: wealth. D3 Drekkana: siblings and courage. D4 Chaturthamsa: home and property. D9 Navamsa: marriage, dharma and inner strength. D10 Dashamsa: career. D12 Dwadashamsa: parents. D16: vehicles and comforts. D20: spiritual practice. D24: learning. D27: strengths and weaknesses. D30: hardships. D40 and D45: maternal and paternal legacy. D60: past karma, the finest division.
Accurate time needed

The finer the division, the faster it changes: D9 every 3 degrees 20 minutes (about 13 minutes of birth time), D60 every half degree (about 2 minutes). Read the fine vargas only with an exact birth time.
Strength across vargas
A planet that is well placed in many vargas is reliable. The Shodashvarga screen shows every planet's sign in each varga side by side.

lessons.title: How to read a chart, step by step
sections: 1. Start with the rising sign
Note the Lagna, its lord, and where that lord sits: this is the core of the person and the direction of life.
2. Read the Moon
Note the Moon's sign, house and nakshatra: this is the mind and emotional life.
3. Scan the houses
See which houses hold planets and which lords sit where. Pay most attention to the 1st, 10th, 7th and 4th houses.
4. Judge strength
Check each planet's dignity, retrogression, combustion and the aspects it receives. Strong planets deliver; weak ones need support.
5. Find the yogas
Look for combinations, then check whether the planets forming them are strong.
6. Time it
Read the running Mahadasha and Antardasha, then the transits of Saturn and Jupiter from the Moon.
7. Confirm with the Navamsa
See whether the D9 supports or weakens what the birth chart shows.
8. Put it together
Look for themes that repeat in several places. A single factor is a hint; three factors pointing the same way are a pattern.
A worked order for one question

For career, for example: look at the 10th house and the planets in it or aspecting it; find the 10th lord and its strength; consider the karakas (the Sun for status, Saturn for work, Mercury for business); check the D10; then see whether the running dasha involves these planets.
Three witnesses
Look for the same promise from the Lagna, from the Moon and in the relevant varga. One witness is a hint, two make it likely, three make it a strong theme.

lessons.title: Using astrology wisely
sections: A tool for understanding
Astrology is best used to understand yourself and to choose good timing, not to live in fear. Difficult placements describe where you grow through effort.
What this app does not do
Some topics are left out on purpose: the app makes no predictions about the length of life or about pregnancy and births.
Remedies
Mantras, charity, fasting and practices are traditional supports, never a substitute for medical, legal or financial advice.
Effort counts
The classical view is that karma from the past (shown by the chart) and effort in the present work together. A difficult period tells you where to put more care, not that effort is useless.
Check the birth time

Before relying on a reading, make sure the birth time is accurate. If two charts a few minutes apart give different rising signs, the house-based readings are uncertain; the Moon and the planets' signs are still reliable.

The 120-year dasha system based on the Moon's nakshatra; the main timing system of Parashari astrology.

About seven and a half years when Saturn passes the 12th, 1st and 2nd signs from the natal Moon.
Aspect: a planet's influence on the houses it looks at.
The angular houses 1, 4, 7 and 10; the pillars of the chart.
The trine houses 1, 5 and 9; the houses of fortune.
The testing houses 6, 8 and 12.
The growth houses 3, 6, 10 and 11, where difficult planets improve with time.

The tenth-division chart (D10), read for career.

The yearly chart cast for the Sun's return to its birth position (Tajika system).
The diamond-style chart picture, in which the houses stay in fixed boxes and the numbers show the signs.
The square chart picture with the signs in fixed boxes, Pisces at the top left, running clockwise.
Conjunction: two or more planets in the same sign and house.
Krishnamurti Paddhati: a modern system based on star lords and sub lords of the house cusps.
A system with fixed houses and practical remedies, separate from Parashari astrology.

picture_guide.heading: What the picture is
picture_guide.text: A birth chart is drawn as a square with twelve boxes. Each box is one house, and each house holds one sign; the planets are written into the box of the sign they were in at birth. The picture is only a map: once you can find the houses, the signs and the planets on it, everything else in the app (lords, aspects, yogas, dashas) can be checked by eye. Two styles are common in India and this app draws both: the North Indian chart and the South Indian chart. They hold exactly the same information, arranged differently.

picture_guide.heading: The North Indian chart: the houses stay in place
picture_guide.text: The North Indian chart is a square crossed by its two diagonals, with a diamond drawn inside by joining the middles of the four sides. That makes four diamonds and eight triangles: twelve boxes. The boxes are the houses and they never move. The diamond at the top centre is always the 1st house, the Lagna. From there the houses run anticlockwise: the 2nd is the triangle at the top left, the 3rd the triangle below it on the left edge, the 4th the diamond on the left, the 5th and 6th the two triangles at the bottom left, the 7th the diamond at the bottom, the 8th and 9th the triangles at the bottom right, the 10th the diamond on the right, and the 11th and 12th the triangles at the top right, ending next to the Lagna.

picture_guide.heading: Four diamonds and eight triangles
picture_guide.text: The shape of a box tells you a lot. The four diamonds are the kendras (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th), the pillars of the chart: a planet in a diamond acts strongly. The 1st, 5th and 9th houses, the trikonas or houses of fortune, form a large triangle on the picture: the top diamond and the lower triangles on the left and right edges. The houses of growth (3rd, 6th, 10th, 11th) and the testing houses (6th, 8th, 12th) are mostly triangles. Opposite boxes face each other across the centre: 1st and 7th, 2nd and 8th, 3rd and 9th, 4th and 10th, 5th and 11th, 6th and 12th.

picture_guide.heading: The small numbers are signs, not houses
picture_guide.text: Each box of a North Indian chart carries a small number. It is the sign in that house, counted from Aries: 1 Aries, 2 Taurus, 3 Gemini, 4 Cancer, 5 Leo, 6 Virgo, 7 Libra, 8 Scorpio, 9 Sagittarius, 10 Capricorn, 11 Aquarius, 12 Pisces. The number in the top diamond is the rising sign: a 6 there means Virgo rising. Going anticlockwise, each box's number is one more than the last, and after 12 comes 1 again. This is the most common beginner's mistake: the house is the position of the box; the number inside is the sign.

picture_guide.heading: Reading one box
picture_guide.text: Inside a box you find the sign number (small) and the planets (bold short names). The 1st house also shows ASC, the Ascendant. The short names used in this app are listed below.

picture_guide.heading: The South Indian chart: the signs stay in place
picture_guide.text: The South Indian chart is a ring of twelve squares round an empty centre (some astrologers write the name and birth details there). Here the boxes are the signs, and they never move: Pisces is always the top-left box, Aries the next one to the right, then Taurus and Gemini along the top, and the signs carry on clockwise round the edge: Cancer and Leo down the right side, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio and Sagittarius along the bottom from right to left, and Capricorn and Aquarius up the left side. Because the signs are fixed, the boxes carry sign names, not numbers.

picture_guide.heading: Finding the houses in a South Indian chart
picture_guide.text: In a South Indian chart the rising sign is marked; in this app its box has a bold border and the word ASC (in printed charts it is often a diagonal line across the box). That box is the 1st house. To find any other house, count clockwise from it, counting the ASC box itself as 1. The 7th house is always the box opposite it, across the centre.

picture_guide.heading: Planets together and apart
picture_guide.text: Planets in the same box share a house and a sign: they are conjunct and colour each other's results. Rahu and Ketu are always in opposite boxes, seven houses apart. An empty box simply has no planet; it is read through its lord. Two planets in one box can still be up to 29 degrees apart; the degrees are on the Kundli Details and planet screens.

picture_guide.heading: Seeing aspects on the picture
picture_guide.text: Every planet looks at (aspects) the box opposite its own, the 7th from it. Mars also looks at the 4th and 8th, Jupiter at the 5th and 9th, and Saturn at the 3rd and 10th. Always count from the planet's own box as 1, in the same direction as the houses: anticlockwise in a North Indian chart, clockwise in a South Indian one.

picture_guide.heading: Following a lord across the picture
picture_guide.text: To find where a house's lord sits: read the sign in that box, recall the sign's lord (Mars for Aries and Scorpio, Venus for Taurus and Libra, Mercury for Gemini and Virgo, the Moon for Cancer, the Sun for Leo, Jupiter for Sagittarius and Pisces, Saturn for Capricorn and Aquarius), then find that planet's short name on the chart. The box it sits in is where that house's matters are carried.

picture_guide.heading: What the picture does not show
picture_guide.text: The picture shows signs, houses and planets only. Degrees, nakshatras, retrograde and combust planets, and strength are not drawn on it; read them on the Kundli Details, Planet by Planet and Planet Strength screens. Some printed charts add an R or brackets for a retrograde planet; this app keeps the picture clean and lists those facts separately.

picture_guide.heading: Divisional charts look the same
picture_guide.text: The Navamsa (D9), the Dashamsa (D10) and the other divisional charts are drawn exactly the same way, each with its own rising sign. Read them with the same steps: find the Lagna, read the sign numbers or names, count the houses from it. Choose a divisional chart on the Chart Diagram screen.

picture_guide.heading: The East Indian chart
picture_guide.text: In Bengal an East Indian style (also called the Bengali chart) is used. Like the South Indian chart it keeps the signs in fixed boxes, but Aries sits in the top centre box and the signs run anticlockwise. The rising sign is marked in its box. This app does not draw the East Indian style, but the reading is the same: find the marked box and count the houses from it in the direction the signs run.

picture_guide.heading: Common mistakes
picture_guide.text: Reading a North Indian sign number as a house number. Counting in the wrong direction: North Indian houses run anticlockwise, South Indian signs run clockwise. Forgetting to count the starting box as 1, which puts every house one box out. Looking for the Lagna in the top-left box of a South Indian chart: that box is always Pisces, whatever the rising sign. Mixing up the birth chart (D1) and the Navamsa (D9) when both are on screen.

picture_guide.heading: Check yourself
picture_guide.text: Open your chart on the Chart Diagram screen and answer these from the picture alone. Then tap the button to see the answers worked out from your chart.

planet_lore.name: Surya
planet_lore.form: Red-gold in colour, with two hands, each holding a lotus. He wears red and a crown, and rides a golden chariot drawn by seven horses, driven by Aruna, the dawn.
planet_lore.story: Surya is the son of the sage Kashyapa and Aditi, the light that sustains all life. He is greeted at sunrise with the Gayatri mantra. Shani and Yama are his sons.

planet_lore.name: Chandra
planet_lore.form: White and calm, with two hands holding a lotus and a mace, a crescent on his crown, riding a chariot drawn by ten white horses.
planet_lore.story: Chandra married the 27 nakshatras, the daughters of Daksha, but loved Rohini most. Daksha's curse made him waste away; Shiva saved him and wore him on his head. So the Moon wanes and waxes every month.

planet_lore.name: Mangala
planet_lore.form: Red, with four arms holding a spear, a trident and a mace, the fourth raised in blessing. He wears red and rides a ram.
planet_lore.story: Mangala is the son of Bhumi Devi, the Earth, and is also called Bhauma, 'born of the Earth'. He is a warrior, the commander of the planets.

planet_lore.name: Budha
planet_lore.form: Yellow-green like the champaka flower, with four arms holding a sword, a shield and a mace, the fourth in blessing. He wears yellow and rides a lion.
planet_lore.story: Budha is the son of Chandra and Tara. Wise and witty, he is the prince among the planets and the patron of learning, speech and trade.

planet_lore.name: Brihaspati
planet_lore.form: Golden yellow, with four arms holding a staff, a rosary and a water pot, the fourth in blessing. He wears yellow and sits on a lotus or rides an elephant.
planet_lore.story: Brihaspati, son of the sage Angiras, is the guru of the gods, their teacher and priest. He is called Guru, the one who removes darkness.

planet_lore.name: Shukra
planet_lore.form: Bright white, with four arms holding a staff, a rosary and a water pot, the fourth in blessing. He wears white and rides a chariot drawn by horses.
planet_lore.story: Shukracharya, son of the sage Bhrigu, is the guru of the asuras. He alone knew the Sanjivani, the knowledge that restores life, and he stands for refinement, art and devotion.

planet_lore.name: Shani
planet_lore.form: Dark blue, lean and austere, with four arms holding a bow, an arrow and a trident, the fourth in blessing. He wears dark clothes and rides a vulture or a crow.
planet_lore.story: Shani is the son of Surya and Chhaya, the Sun's shadow-wife. He moves slowest of all and is the judge who rewards patience and honest work. He is honoured on Saturdays.

planet_lore.name: Rahu
planet_lore.form: Smoky dark with a fierce face, four arms holding a sword, a shield and a trident, the fourth in blessing, riding a lion; often shown as a head alone, rising from dark clouds.
planet_lore.story: At the churning of the ocean the asura Svarbhanu sat among the gods and drank the nectar of immortality. The Sun and Moon saw him and Vishnu cut off his head with the Sudarshana disc. The immortal head became Rahu, who chases the Sun and Moon and swallows them at eclipses.

planet_lore.name: Ketu
planet_lore.form: Smoky grey, with two arms holding a mace, the other in blessing, riding a vulture; the body ends in a serpent's tail and a banner flies above.
planet_lore.story: Ketu is the body of Svarbhanu, separated from the head. Without a head he stands for detachment, insight and liberation; his name means 'banner' and also 'comet'.
